passages.text: For instance, Simon, who is to debate with us tomorrow, dares to argue publicly against God’s sole rule, intending to bring forward many statements from the Scriptures themselves to the effect that there are many gods and that a certain one—not the one who created the world—is higher than the latter; and correspondingly he can furnish written proofs. We too can clearly point out many passages from the same Scriptures showing that this one, the one who created the world, is the one God, and that “there is no other except him.” Yet if anyone wishes to speak in some other way, he too will be able to provide proofs from them, in whatever way he wishes and about whatever he wishes. For the Scriptures say everything, so that none of those who search ungratefully may find the truth, but rather what he wants, while the truth is reserved for the grateful. Gratitude consists in preserving intact one’s affection for the one responsible for our existence.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase introduces Simon as an immediate illustration of the preceding general claim; “at any rate, immediately” would preserve the particles more formally.
Renders μοναρχία as the rule of one rather than using a modern political label.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πολλὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν τῶν γραφῶν φωνὰς ἐνεγκεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: to bring forward many statements from the Scriptures themselves
lexical_decisions.rationale: φωναί literally means voices or utterances; “statements” fits citations taken from written texts while preserving their asserted content.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἷς δέ τις οὐχ ὁ τὸν κόσμον κτίσας τούτου ἀνώτερος
lexical_decisions.chosen: a certain one—not the one who created the world—is higher than the latter
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text takes τούτου to refer to the world-creator. It could grammatically refer instead to the world, yielding “higher than this world.” The creator-reference is chosen because the surrounding argument contrasts the creator with an allegedly superior god, and the following sentence identifies the creator as the one God.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ὁμῶς τὰς ἀποδείξεις ἐγγράφους ἔχει παρασχεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: and correspondingly he can furnish written proofs
lexical_decisions.rationale: The printed ὁμῶς means “equally” or “likewise,” hence “correspondingly.” “Nevertheless” would normally represent differently accented ὅμως and is not adopted.
περικοπαί are portions or sections cut from a larger text, naturally rendered here as scriptural passages.
ἀγνωμόνως may also mean without judgment or unreasonably. The author’s immediate definition of εὐγνωμοσύνη as preserving affection for one’s benefactor supports the gratitude sense here.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα μηδεὶς τῶν ἀγνωμόνως ζητούντων τὸ ἀληθὲς εὕρῃ, ἀλλ’ ὃ βούλεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that none of those who search ungratefully may find the truth, but rather what he wants
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text takes τὸ ἀληθές as the object of εὕρῃ, in contrast with the second object, ὃ βούλεται. It is also grammatically possible to attach τὸ ἀληθές to ζητούντων and understand an unstated object for εὕρῃ: “those who search for the truth ungratefully may not find it, but rather what they want.” The explicit contrast between the two objects favors the chosen attachment.

lexical_decisions.chosen: while the truth is reserved for the grateful
lexical_decisions.rationale: εὐγνώμων can mean right-minded, fair, or grateful. “Grateful” maintains the contrast with ἀγνωμόνως and anticipates the next sentence’s definition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εὐγνωμοσύνη δέ ἐστιν τὸ τὴν πρὸς τὸν τοῦ εἶναι ἡμᾶς αἴτιον ἀποσώζειν στοργήν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Gratitude consists in preserving intact one’s affection for the one responsible for our existence
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀποσώζειν conveys keeping or preserving safely and intact. “Gratitude” fits the benefactor relationship expressed by affection toward the cause of human existence, though “right-mindedness” remains a lexical alternative.
